Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1a) demonstrates a widened superior mediastinum consistent with an anterior mediastinal mass (thymic carcinoma), and the trachea appears midline without significant displacement. Thymic malignancies are known to invade or compress adjacent structures, including the phrenic nerve, leading to diaphragmatic palsy, which fits the clinical profile better than the other options describing posterior/middle locations or obvious tracheal deviation.
